questions.question: A specialty coffee roaster's roast-profile software is licensed per host, requires one specific operating system build, and is supported by its vendor only while the roaster controls the host itself. The roaster wants this workload running in Google Cloud without renegotiating any of that. Which product should it land on?

options.A: Compute Engine, where the roaster runs and controls its own virtual machines
options.B: Cloud Run, which runs the roaster's container with no servers to manage
options.C: GKE, which would orchestrate the software's containers across a cluster
options.D: A managed service replacing the roast-profile software altogether

rationale.correct: Some constraints keep a workload on virtual machines: licensing tied to a host, one required operating system build, and vendor support conditioned on controlling the machine. Compute Engine is the product for exactly that, since the roaster runs its own virtual machines with full control of the operating system, and it is the natural landing place for a lift and shift.

distractors.B: A serverless container platform removes the servers the roaster is required to control, and the vendor's support terms are written around that control.
distractors.C: Orchestrating containers assumes the software has been containerized, which is a change both the license and the support terms push back on.
distractors.D: Replacing the software answers a different question, since the roaster asked how to move this workload without renegotiating anything and a replacement renegotiates everything.

keywords: accelerated deployment processes through managed services
questions.question: A stock photography marketplace is writing the business case for modernizing its application estate. The board has already accepted the cost argument and has asked for two further outcomes, stated in business terms, that are not about spending less. Select the TWO outcomes that belong in that section.

options.A: Cost optimization, with capacity paid for only while it is actually in use
options.B: A smaller operations team once the modernized estate is running
options.C: Enhanced scalability and resilience, so peaks and failures stop being incidents
options.D: A faster page load for every visitor browsing the marketplace
options.E: Faster deployment through managed services, so features reach customers sooner

rationale.correct: Modern application development is argued in outcomes. Enhanced scalability and resilience means demand peaks and failures stop being incidents, and accelerated deployment processes through managed services means features reach customers sooner because nobody is operating the platform underneath them. Cost optimization, flexible architectures like microservices and improved operational efficiency are the other outcomes on that list.

distractors.A: Paying only for capacity in use is cost optimization, and the board has said the cost argument is already accepted.
distractors.B: Modernizing changes what an operations team spends its time on, and a smaller team is a promise the approach does not make and a business case should not carry.
distractors.D: A faster page is a technical improvement that may well follow, and it is not one of the business outcomes this section was asked to state.

questions.question: A textile mill runs forty containerized services with hand-written Kubernetes manifests, node pools sized per service, and a scheduling policy its platform team maintains deliberately. The team is content to keep owning all of that. What it will not keep doing is patching and upgrading the Kubernetes control plane itself. Which product fits?

options.A: Cloud Run, which removes cluster concepts from the team's work entirely
options.B: Compute Engine, with the team still running Kubernetes on its own machines
options.C: Cloud Run functions for each service, triggered by the events they handle
options.D: GKE, which runs the control plane while the team keeps its manifests and policy

rationale.correct: The team has been explicit about what it keeps and what it hands over: manifests, node pools and scheduling policy stay, and the control plane goes. GKE is managed Kubernetes at exactly that line, with Google operating the control plane while the team retains orchestration control, which is the abstraction a containerized estate with deliberate policy needs.

distractors.A: A serverless container platform takes the cluster away along with the control plane, and the mill's node pools and scheduling policy are the parts it deliberately keeps.
distractors.B: Running Kubernetes on the mill's own machines leaves the control plane precisely where it is, which is the one part of the job the team has said it will not keep doing.
distractors.C: Rebuilding forty long-running services as event-triggered functions is a re-architecture nobody asked for, and it discards the orchestration control the team maintains on purpose.

questions.question: A veterinary clinic network's two developers have built a booking service in a language of their own choosing and packaged it as a container so it behaves identically on their laptops. Traffic is spiky during clinic hours and near zero overnight. They want to keep their language and tooling and to manage no infrastructure at all. Which product fits?

options.A: GKE, which would run the container on a cluster the developers configure
options.B: Cloud Run, which runs their container with no infrastructure to manage
options.C: Compute Engine, with the container started by a script on a virtual machine
options.D: A shared server in the network's head office, hosting the service internally

rationale.correct: Cloud Run leaves the language and tooling choice with the developers and takes over everything below the container: the container is the unit of deployment, the platform runs and scales it, and nothing is left running when traffic falls away. Two developers who have already packaged their own container and want to manage no infrastructure describe that product precisely.

distractors.A: A managed cluster still has to be configured and maintained, which is infrastructure management under another name and more than two developers should be carrying.
distractors.C: Starting the container with a script on a virtual machine leaves the network operating that machine, patching it, and paying for it through every quiet night.
distractors.D: Hosting the service on a head-office server puts clinic booking traffic on hardware nobody is scaling, and a spiky pattern is what that arrangement handles worst.

questions.question: Whenever a student uploads a certificate scan into a vocational training institute's document store, a short piece of code must stamp it with an audit reference and notify the registrar. The code runs for a second or two, fires a few dozen times a day, and does so at unpredictable moments. Where should that code run?

options.A: On a Compute Engine instance kept running so it is ready for each upload
options.B: On the GKE cluster the institute already operates for its learning portal
options.C: On Cloud Run functions, triggered by the upload event itself
options.D: In a nightly batch that stamps and notifies for all of the day's uploads

rationale.correct: Small pieces of code that run in response to events belong on Cloud Run functions: the upload is the trigger, the code runs for as long as it takes, and nothing is kept running in between. A cluster or a virtual machine held ready for work that fires a few dozen times a day is capacity paid for and idle almost all of it.

distractors.A: An instance kept running is billed through every hour when nothing is uploaded, and the institute would own its patching and its capacity as well.
distractors.B: The learning portal's cluster can certainly run the code, and it brings orchestration this task never needs while still leaving someone to operate it.
distractors.D: A nightly batch means a certificate uploaded in the morning carries no audit reference all day, and the registrar hears about it a day late.

questions.question: A waste management utility has bid for a municipal contract whose terms require the collection data to stay on the rival cloud the council already uses, while the utility's own analytics stay on Google Cloud. The utility will not run two analytics stacks. Which capability lets its analysts query the data held on the other provider?

options.A: BigQuery Omni, which runs BigQuery analytics against data in other clouds
options.B: Cloud Interconnect, giving a private network link between the two environments
options.C: A scheduled copy of the other cloud's data into BigQuery every night
options.D: GKE Enterprise, which manages Kubernetes clusters across both cloud providers

rationale.correct: Some products follow an organization off Google Cloud: BigQuery Omni runs analytics against data held in other clouds, AlloyDB Omni runs the database engine in other environments, GKE Enterprise spans fleets, and Cloud SQL and Looker connect across clouds. The requirement here is analytics reach over data that has to stay elsewhere, which is what BigQuery Omni answers without a second stack.

distractors.B: A private link moves packets between environments and answers nothing about where a query runs or which engine the analysts work in.
distractors.C: Copying the data every night takes it out of the environment the contract requires it to stay in, and it makes every answer a day old.
distractors.D: Managing clusters across providers is the same idea applied to container workloads, and this utility's problem is analytics rather than where its clusters run.

questions.question: A wind-farm operator is commissioning a new maintenance-scheduling application that must read turbine availability from a twenty-year-old control system nobody intends to replace. The project brief says the two will be joined by an API. In plain terms, what is the operator's board being told?

options.A: That the turbine data will be copied into the new application's own store
options.B: That the new application will ask the existing system for data in an agreed way
options.C: That the control system's hardware will be managed from the new application
options.D: That both systems will move onto one platform so they share a single store

rationale.correct: An application programming interface is the agreed way one system asks another for something. It is the connector between a new application and an existing system: the maintenance scheduler asks, the control system answers, and neither has to be rebuilt or replaced for that to work.

distractors.A: Copying the data into a second store is a different integration approach and leaves two copies to keep in step, where an interface asks the source each time.
distractors.C: Managing hardware is not what an interface does. The connection carries requests and answers, and the turbine control equipment stays exactly where it is.
distractors.D: Moving both systems onto one platform is a migration program, and the operator has said the control system is not being replaced.

questions.question: A regional tourism board has spent years assembling an accommodation and events dataset that hotel booking sites, map applications and airlines all keep asking for by email. Its finance committee wants a proposal for turning those requests into income. What should the proposal recommend?

options.A: Publishing the dataset as a free download so the requests stop arriving
options.B: Licensing a nightly export to each requester under an individual contract
options.C: Building a public website where visitors can search the dataset themselves
options.D: Exposing and monetizing a public-facing API that partners call directly

rationale.correct: An interface can be a product rather than plumbing. Exposing and monetizing public-facing APIs turns a capability the board already has into something partners pay to call, which is how internal data opens new business opportunities instead of generating email traffic.

distractors.A: A free download ends the requests and the income together, which is the opposite of what the finance committee asked for.
distractors.B: Individually negotiated exports do earn money, and each new partner needs its own contract and its own file, so the arrangement stops paying as demand grows.
distractors.C: A public search site serves visitors, and the demand described comes from businesses that want the data inside their own products.

questions.question: A ceramics manufacturer already exposes an ordering interface that a dozen distributors call. It now wants to open the same interface to hundreds of independent retailers, with per-partner credentials, rate limits, published documentation and a record of who called what. Its two backend engineers cannot build all of that. What should the manufacturer adopt?

options.A: Cloud Armor, to protect the interface from abusive traffic at the Google Cloud edge
options.B: A second copy of the ordering service, sized for the retailers' traffic
options.C: Apigee API Management, which publishes, secures and meters the interface
options.D: One shared credential issued to all retailers, with usage reviewed monthly

rationale.correct: An interface and the management layer around it are different things. Apigee API Management is that layer: it publishes the interface with documentation, secures it with per-partner credentials, meters and rate-limits its use, and analyzes usage at scale, which is the work two backend engineers would otherwise have to build and then operate forever.

distractors.A: Edge protection blocks abusive traffic, and it issues no partner credentials, publishes no documentation and meters nothing.
distractors.B: A second copy of the service adds capacity to a problem that is about governing hundreds of callers, and it doubles what the two engineers maintain.
distractors.D: One credential shared by hundreds of retailers cannot be rate-limited per partner or revoked for one of them, and a monthly review finds the misuse after it has happened.

questions.question: A credit union's servers slowed steadily over three months. No ransom was demanded, no records were altered and nothing appeared in public, but electricity use climbed sharply and a scan eventually found unauthorized software consuming spare processing capacity around the clock. Which threat class does this describe?

options.A: Ransomware, whose payload had not yet announced its demand
options.B: Cryptomining, which quietly steals computing capacity and demands nothing
options.C: Misconfiguration, as spare capacity was left available for anything to use
options.D: A distributed denial-of-service attack, which is what slowed the servers

rationale.correct: Threat classes are named from how they behave. Cryptomining steals computing capacity and stays silent, because the longer it goes unnoticed the more it earns, which fits servers that slow steadily while electricity use climbs and nothing is demanded, altered or published. Ransomware announces itself, malware and viruses are the wider family of silent theft and damage, and DDoS overwhelms from outside.

distractors.A: Ransomware exists to be noticed, given that a demand nobody sees earns nothing, and three months of quiet degradation is the opposite of that behavior.
distractors.C: Misconfiguration belongs to the exposures an organization inflicts on itself, and unauthorized software installed and running is somebody else's deliberate act.
distractors.D: A denial-of-service flood arrives from outside and stops when it stops. It installs nothing, and it does not explain software running on the servers around the clock.

questions.question: A cinema chain runs an AI assistant that answers customer questions by reading the chain's own help articles. A contributor added a sentence to one article instructing the assistant to reveal other customers' booking references, and on the next question the assistant did exactly that. Which layer of the AI stack must the chain secure against this class of attack?

options.A: The data layer, where content the model reads is validated before it is trusted
options.B: The infrastructure layer, by hardening the machines the model runs on
options.C: The model layer, by retraining the assistant on examples of harmful instructions
options.D: The platform layer, by adding a notice that answers are generated by AI

rationale.correct: LLM attacks reach a system through untrusted input to a model, and this instruction arrived inside a help article the assistant reads as source material. Defending it means securing the layer where untrusted content enters, which is the data layer; the infrastructure, models, platform and agents layers each defend something else.

distractors.B: Hardened machines protect the compute a model runs on, and this hostile text arrived through content the assistant was designed to read.
distractors.C: Retraining shifts the odds a little and leaves the mechanism intact, as the article still carries an instruction the assistant reads as legitimate source material.
distractors.D: Telling customers that answers are generated does not stop booking references being disclosed; it explains where the disclosure came from.

questions.question: A national postal service's audit committee asks its security lead what genuinely changes when the parcel-tracking estate moves out of the service's own data center and onto Google Cloud. Which answer should the security lead give?

options.A: Responsibility passes to the provider, so the service's own duties end
options.B: Nothing of substance changes, since the same controls apply in the same way
options.C: Responsibility is shared, and the service's main exposure becomes configuration
options.D: Physical security stops mattering once no hardware belongs to the service

rationale.correct: Cloud security differs from on-premises security in three genuine ways: responsibility is shared rather than wholly the customer's, the provider operates a security baseline the postal service could not run at that scale, and the service's largest remaining exposure becomes how it configures what it deploys. What does not change is that the service still owns its data, its access decisions and its obligations.

distractors.A: Shared responsibility is not transferred responsibility, and the service keeps its data, its access decisions and every obligation a regulator holds it to.
distractors.B: Treating the move as a change of address misses the shift: the provider now operates layers the service used to run, and misconfiguration replaces hardware as the main way things go wrong.
distractors.D: Physical security still matters and is now performed by the provider, which makes it part of the baseline the service inherits rather than a concern that disappears.

questions.question: A garden centre chain discovers that a nightly job has silently corrupted three months of loyalty-point balances. No data left the company, the systems stayed usable throughout, and no regulator or contractual requirement is engaged. Which property of the chain's security model failed?

options.A: Confidentiality, which keeps information from reaching the wrong people
options.B: Availability, which keeps the service usable when customers need it
options.C: Compliance, which is engaged whenever customer records are affected
options.D: Integrity, which keeps data accurate and unaltered except by intent

rationale.correct: Each property answers a different question. Integrity asks whether data is accurate and unaltered except by intended change, and a job that silently corrupted three months of balances broke exactly that. Confidentiality would have failed if data had reached the wrong people, availability if the service had stopped, compliance if an obligation had been breached, and control concerns who makes the decisions.

distractors.A: Confidentiality is about disclosure, and the scenario states that no data left the company.
distractors.B: Availability is about the service being usable, and the systems stayed usable throughout the corruption.
distractors.C: An obligation has to exist and be breached before compliance is the failed property, and none is engaged here.

questions.question: A wine importer and distributor's warehouse application is reachable only from inside the corporate network, and anything that reaches it is treated as trusted. After a contractor's laptop was compromised on that network and used to pull stock records, the security lead proposes that every request be verified whatever its origin. Which principle is being proposed?

options.A: Zero-trust architecture, which verifies every request regardless of origin
options.B: Least privilege, granting each account only what its task requires
options.C: Privileged access management, controlling the administrator accounts
options.D: A firewall rule blocking contractor devices from the warehouse application

rationale.correct: The three terms restrict different things. Zero-trust architecture removes the assumption that being inside the network confers trust, verifying every request whatever its origin, which is precisely the assumption the compromised laptop exploited. Least privilege limits what an account may do once it is trusted, and privileged access is the narrower discipline of managing exceptional accounts.

distractors.B: Least privilege narrows what each account can reach and still allows an account on the corporate network to be trusted merely for being there.
distractors.C: Managing administrator accounts is real work and a smaller part of this problem, as the contractor's laptop needed no administrator rights to be trusted by the application.
distractors.D: Blocking one class of device answers this incident and leaves the assumption intact, so the next compromised machine on that network is trusted exactly as the last one was.

questions.question: A municipal fire service passed an external penetration test in January and has treated that certificate as its security position ever since. The new head of technology argues that a test result is a photograph rather than a position, and asks the leadership team to fund something different. What should the service recognize?

options.A: That the penetration test should be repeated monthly rather than annually
options.B: That the certificate should be published so partners can see the result
options.C: That security posture is a continuing state, maintained by security operations
options.D: That a stronger firewall would raise the score at the next penetration test

rationale.correct: Security posture is the state of a system rather than a certificate about it, and security by default and cyber resilience describe properties a system holds continuously. Security operations is the discipline that keeps posture honest, using threat intelligence to see what is coming and threat response to deal with what arrives, which is exactly what a point-in-time test cannot do.

distractors.A: A more frequent test produces more photographs, and between them the service is still relying on a past result instead of a state it maintains.
distractors.B: Publishing the certificate tells partners what was true in January and changes nothing about what is true today.
distractors.D: A control change aimed at the next test optimizes for the test, and posture is what holds between tests rather than on the day of one.

questions.question: A campus bookstore chain's board asks which product it has to buy in order to encrypt the student purchase records it is about to store in Google Cloud, and how long enabling that product will take. What should the chief information officer tell the board?

options.A: Sensitive Data Protection must be enabled first, so records are found and encrypted
options.B: Nothing needs buying: data stored on Google Cloud is encrypted at rest by default
options.C: A firewall rule must be applied first so only the chain's systems can read the records
options.D: Encryption applies once each bucket is tagged as holding sensitive records

rationale.correct: Encryption at rest is the default state of data on Google Cloud, inherited from secure-by-design core infrastructure, which includes proprietary data centers, purpose-built servers and networking, and custom security hardware and software. It is not switched on by a purchase. Data loss prevention, firewalls, and encryption and decryption are distinct jobs, and only the first two are things the chain chooses to apply.

distractors.A: Sensitive Data Protection discovers and classifies sensitive data, which is a different job from encrypting it, and the records are already encrypted at rest without it.
distractors.C: A firewall rule governs what can reach the records over the network and performs no encryption, so it answers a different question than the board asked.
distractors.D: Encryption at rest is not conditioned on a tag or on any other customer action; it is the state the data is already in.

questions.question: A physiotherapy clinic chain's assessment confirms that patient notes are encrypted on disk and encrypted while moving between the clinics and the central system. The remaining concern is the moment the central system loads a note into memory to run its analysis, on infrastructure shared with other tenants. Which state of data is that concern about?

options.A: Data at rest, which is where the stored notes are protected
options.B: Data in transit, which is where notes moving between systems are protected
options.C: No further state applies once data is encrypted on disk and on the wire
options.D: Data in use, the state a note is in while it is being processed

rationale.correct: Encryption controls are matched to the state the data is in. At rest covers what sits on disk, in transit covers what moves between systems, and in use covers data while it is being processed. The clinic chain has covered the first two states, and the exposure it now describes is the third.

distractors.A: At rest is one of the states already covered, since the notes are encrypted on disk before anything reads them.
distractors.B: In transit is the other state already covered, protecting notes as they move between the clinics and the central system.
distractors.C: Data being processed is a recognized state with protection of its own, which is why it is named alongside at rest and in transit rather than folded into them.

questions.question: A radio broadcasting network's incident review finds that a producer signed in with a valid credential, satisfied the network's multi-factor challenge, and then deleted a broadcast archive that nobody in that role should ever have been able to delete. The network's logs recorded every step. Which of the three A's failed here?

options.A: Authorization, which decides what an identity is permitted to do
options.B: Authentication, which proves an identity is who it claims to be
options.C: Auditing, which records what each identity actually did
options.D: Two-step verification, which should have been required for the deletion

rationale.correct: The three A's answer different questions. Authentication proves who you are, and multi-factor authentication and two-step verification are how it is strengthened; authorization decides what you may do, and IAM grants it through roles; auditing records what you did. A valid sign-in that reached a capability the role should never have held is an authorization failure.

distractors.B: Authentication did its job as designed, since the sign-in used a valid credential and the multi-factor challenge was satisfied.
distractors.C: Auditing also worked, which is how the review knows what happened, and recording an action is not the same as preventing it.
distractors.D: Another verification step at sign-in would have proved the producer's identity once more and left that role's permissions exactly as they were.

questions.question: A motorway toll operator's security team learns about new attack techniques only when its own monitoring catches one in progress. The team wants insight into what is coming before it arrives, and asks what Google Threat Intelligence would add. What is the accurate answer?

options.A: It detects threats inside the operator's estate faster than current monitoring does
options.B: It certifies the operator's controls against a recognized external security standard
options.C: It gives proactive insight into threats from three different kinds of source
options.D: It scores each threat with a severity index published by an industry consortium

rationale.correct: Threat intelligence is proactive: it tells an organization what is coming rather than what is already inside. Google Threat Intelligence draws on three sources that differ in kind, namely Google's vast global visibility, Mandiant's frontline incident response expertise, and VirusTotal's crowd sourced threat detection, which is why together they see more than any one of them could alone.

distractors.A: Detecting what is already in the estate is the job of a security operations platform, and the team's complaint is that detection is the only warning it ever gets.
distractors.B: Certification against a standard is assurance about controls, and it says nothing about which techniques attackers are using this month.
distractors.D: No such consortium index is part of this offering, and one score would flatten exactly the differences in kind that make three sources worth combining.

questions.question: An artisan food cooperative's security review finds two gaps. First, nobody can say which of its projects have publicly exposed storage or over-broad roles. Second, when an alert does fire, the telemetry sits in five separate consoles and nobody correlates it. Which product addresses the first gap?

options.A: Google Security Operations, which unifies telemetry with detection
options.B: Security Command Center, which finds and prioritizes misconfigurations
options.C: Cloud Logging, which would collect the projects' logs in one place
options.D: A quarterly manual review of each project's roles and storage buckets

rationale.correct: The two gaps belong to two products. Security Command Center is the posture product: it discovers, prioritizes and remediates misconfigurations before an attacker finds them, which is what unknown exposure across projects needs. Google Security Operations is the unified security operations platform that ingests telemetry and drives threat detection and response, which is what the second gap needs.

distractors.A: Unifying telemetry and correlating alerts answers the cooperative's second gap, and it starts from signals that something is already happening.
distractors.C: Collecting logs in one place is a useful step toward the second gap and finds no exposed bucket by itself, as a log records what happened rather than what is misconfigured.
distractors.D: A manual sweep discovers exposures at most four times a year and only where somebody thought to look, which is detection after the fact rather than continuous posture.

questions.question: A heavy-equipment leasing firm's security team has two requests on its desk. The rental business wants its new customer-facing AI assistant protected from hostile prompts. The security team itself wants its analysts to triage alerts faster with AI assistance. Which pairing meets both requests?

options.A: Gemini in Google Security Operations for the assistant, and AI Protection for triage
options.B: Model Armor for both requests, as the single offering that covers anything involving AI
options.C: Cloud Armor for the assistant, and Google Security Command Center for alert triage
options.D: Model Armor for the assistant, and Gemini in Google Security Operations for triage

rationale.correct: Securing AI and securing with AI are two different offerings. AI Protection and Model Armor defend AI systems themselves, which is what a customer-facing assistant exposed to hostile prompts needs. Gemini in Google Security Operations puts AI to work defending everything else, which is what analysts triaging alerts need.

distractors.A: These are the right two offerings pointed the wrong way round, with the analyst assistance aimed at the model and the model defense aimed at the analysts.
distractors.B: Defending a model covers one of the two requests and leaves the analysts where they started, as protecting an assistant does nothing to speed up alert triage.
distractors.C: Edge traffic protection and posture management are real products for other jobs, and neither of them inspects what a customer types into an assistant.

questions.question: A public library system has two obligations from its latest audit. Branch staff must reach an internal lending application from home without any network-level connection to the corporate estate, and the system must establish whether borrower records containing national identity numbers have been copied into shared spreadsheets. Select the TWO products that meet these obligations.

options.A: Cloud Armor, defending the lending application from hostile traffic at the edge
options.B: Identity-Aware Proxy, gating access to the application on verified identity
options.C: Confidential Computing, protecting the records while they are being processed
options.D: Sensitive Data Protection, discovering where sensitive records have spread
options.E: Record Scanner, the built-in service that lists identity numbers per project

rationale.correct: Each obligation names its product. Reaching an internal application without a network connection is identity-gated access, which is Identity-Aware Proxy, and establishing where sensitive records have spread is sensitive-data discovery, which is Sensitive Data Protection. Cloud VPC, Cloud VPN, Cloud Interconnect, firewalls, Cloud Armor, Cloud Logging, IAM, Confidential Computing and Certificate Manager each answer a different obligation in the same family.

distractors.A: Edge defense keeps hostile traffic away from an application and grants no member of branch staff access to it from home.
distractors.C: Protecting data while it is processed is a real control at a different point: it guards records in use and finds none of the copies already sitting in spreadsheets.
distractors.E: No product of that name exists in this family, and the discovery work it describes belongs to Sensitive Data Protection.

questions.question: An auction house's insurer will underwrite a move to a cloud provider only if the provider's security claims can be evidenced rather than asserted. The provider's sales team offers a summary of its security architecture and a reference call with another customer. What should the auction house ask for instead?

options.A: Transparency reports, third-party audit results and the compliance resource manager
options.B: A contractual warranty that the provider's controls operate as described
options.C: A demonstration of the Security Command Center console by its solutions engineer
options.D: An architecture document explaining how the provider's controls are designed and layered

rationale.correct: Trust is evidenced rather than asserted. Transparency reports show what the provider has actually done, third-party audits record an independent party's finding rather than the provider's own account, and the compliance resource manager collects the certifications a customer can hand to its insurer. A vendor claim, however detailed, is still the vendor speaking about itself.

distractors.B: A warranty allocates the consequences if the claims turn out to be false, and the insurer has asked for proof that they are true.
distractors.C: A guided demonstration shows what a console looks like on the day it is shown, which is the vendor speaking about itself with better visuals.
distractors.D: An architecture document describes how controls are designed, and evidence concerns whether they operate, which only an independent finding establishes.

questions.question: A customs brokerage wins a government contract whose terms require declaration records to remain within the country's borders and not to be disclosable to any foreign authority. The brokerage's security team reports that the records are encrypted and access-controlled. Which concern does the contract raise that the team's report leaves unanswered?

options.A: Whether the encryption keys protecting the declaration records are strong enough
options.B: Whether an attacker could reach the declaration records through a misconfigured storage bucket
options.C: Digital sovereignty and data residency: where records sit and whose law reaches them
options.D: Whether the brokerage's staff have been cleared to handle government records

rationale.correct: Encryption and access control answer who can read the records. Digital sovereignty and data residency answer a different question entirely: where the data physically lives, which country's law reaches it, and who could be compelled to hand it over. Neither is a question about a threat actor, and no security control settles either one.

distractors.A: Key strength is a control setting and a matter for the security report, and a perfectly encrypted record held in the wrong jurisdiction still breaches the contract.
distractors.B: A misconfigured bucket is a genuine exposure to an attacker, and the contract's concern is a lawful demand rather than an unlawful one.
distractors.D: Staff clearance governs who inside the brokerage may handle the records, which leaves untouched the question of which government could compel their disclosure.

questions.question: An industrial bakery's finance director compares five years of cloud subscription against the purchase price of the replacement servers the estate would otherwise need, and concludes that the cloud is the more expensive option. The IT manager replies that the comparison is not a like-for-like one. Which comparison would be honest?

options.A: Add the electricity, cooling and server-room space to the purchase price
options.B: Compare only the cash leaving the business each year under either option
options.C: Treat the two as equivalent, as the same workload runs under either one
options.D: Count hardware investment, operational overhead and opportunity cost together

rationale.correct: Adopting cloud moves spend from capital expenditures (CapEx) toward operational expenditures (OpEx), and a total cost of ownership (TCO) comparison is honest only when it counts hardware investment, operational overhead and opportunity cost together. Any one of them alone flatters a side: purchase price ignores what running the estate costs, and both ignore what the bakery's people could have been doing instead.

distractors.A: Power, cooling and floor space are real operational overhead and one part of the picture, and a comparison that stops there still omits what the estate costs in people and in forgone work.
distractors.B: Cash leaving the business each year is a treasury view rather than a cost of ownership, and it hides the capital already sunk into hardware the bakery owns.
distractors.C: The same workload does not cost the same to run in both places, which is the whole reason the comparison is being made.

questions.question: A private university's cloud spend has doubled in a year. Each faculty runs its own projects, a central dashboard already shows every cost down to the service, and no faculty head has ever been asked to explain a rise. The finance committee wants cloud financial governance that actually works. Select the TWO changes that would establish it.

options.A: Each project's owner is also made accountable for what that project spends
options.B: A monthly report of the largest-spending projects is circulated to the deans
options.C: Every faculty is given the same fixed budget regardless of what it runs
options.D: A better cost dashboard is bought so that the figures are easier to read
options.E: A standing review is established, with named people and agreed thresholds

rationale.correct: Cloud financial governance answers who manages cloud costs, and it works through people, process, and technology together. Pairing each project's ownership with financial accountability gives the spend a named owner, and a standing review with named people and agreed thresholds is the process that makes the ownership operate. Visibility on its own changes nothing while nobody is answerable for what it shows.

distractors.B: A circulated report tells the deans what has already been spent, and the university's problem is that nobody is ever asked to account for it.
distractors.C: One fixed budget across faculties ignores what each of them actually runs, starving the heavy workloads and leaving the light ones with headroom nobody watches.
distractors.D: The university already has a dashboard showing every cost, so a clearer one is technology answering a question about people and process.

questions.question: A museum and heritage trust must apply one data-retention policy to everything its digital preservation department runs, without anyone having to set it on each new project as it is created. The department's work sits in a dozen projects today and will spread into more. Other departments must not be bound by this policy. Where should it be applied?

options.A: On each project as it is created, so every project's policy is explicit
options.B: On a folder holding the department's projects, so new projects inherit it
options.C: On the organization node, so the whole trust is covered in one action
options.D: In a documented standard that every project owner is asked to follow

rationale.correct: The hierarchy runs resources inside projects, projects inside folders, and folders under the organization node, each element having exactly one parent. What the tree buys is inheritance and propagation: a policy set on a folder reaches every project beneath it, including projects that do not exist yet, which is precisely what the trust asked for.

distractors.A: Setting the policy on each project is the work the trust asked to avoid, and every project created next year starts without it until somebody remembers.
distractors.C: The organization node does cover the department, and it also binds every other part of the trust to a retention rule written for digital preservation.
distractors.D: A written standard depends on each owner reading and following it, and nothing in the hierarchy enforces it, so the first project that skips it is invisible.

questions.question: A textile mill's finance team has two distinct cost problems. A research team occasionally launches far more machines than anyone expected, and separately the monthly pattern-simulation run is simply expensive at list price, although it can wait days for capacity. Which pairing of controls addresses both problems?

options.A: Budget threshold rules for both problems, as alerts cover overspend of any kind
options.B: Resource quota policies for the simulation run, and Compute Engine Spot VMs for the research team
options.C: Cloud Billing reports for both, so the finance team can see where the money goes
options.D: Resource quota policies for the research team, and Dynamic Workload Scheduler for the run

rationale.correct: The two problems need different kinds of control. Unexpected launches are capped before the money is spent, which is what resource quota policies and budget threshold rules do. A job that is expensive by nature and can wait is instead bought on the platform's terms, which is what Dynamic Workload Scheduler and Spot VMs are for.

distractors.A: Budget threshold rules would tell the mill that the research team has overspent, and they do nothing about the price of a run that is expensive by design.
distractors.B: The two controls are pointed at the wrong problems, as a quota on a scheduled run does not make it cheaper and interruptible capacity does not stop a team launching too much.
distractors.C: Billing reports answer where the money went, which is analysis rather than control, and neither problem is that the finance team cannot see the spend.

questions.question: A language school network's board wants to know which of its cost centres drove last quarter's increase and which services the money went on, before it decides anything at all. No decision has yet been taken about caps, commitments or discounts. Which capability answers the board's question?

options.A: Cloud Billing reports, which show what was spent and where it went
options.B: Budget threshold rules, which alert when spend passes a set level
options.C: Resource quota policies, which cap what each project may consume
options.D: Spot VMs, which lower the price of the network's batch workloads

rationale.correct: The board has asked an analysis question: what was spent, by whom, and on which services. Cloud Billing reports answer exactly that. Controls that cap consumption and mechanisms that discount it both act on future spend, and neither explains a quarter that has already closed.

distractors.B: A threshold alert fires when spend crosses a level and reports nothing about which cost centre or which service drove a quarter that has already closed.
distractors.C: A quota limits what a project may consume from now on, so it shapes the next quarter and explains nothing about the last one.
distractors.D: Cheaper capacity for batch work reduces future bills, and the board has asked what happened rather than what to change.

questions.question: A parcel locker network's checkout has become slow, and its dashboards show every individual service comfortably inside its own latency limits. The team needs to see where the time actually goes across the chain of services that one checkout request passes through. Which product answers that?

options.A: Cloud Monitoring, which would chart each service's latency metrics
options.B: Cloud Logging, which would let the team search each service's logs
options.C: Cloud Trace, which follows one request through the services it visits
options.D: Cloud Profiler, which shows where a service's code consumes resources

rationale.correct: Each product in Google Cloud's Observability answers a different operational question. Cloud Monitoring charts metrics, Cloud Logging searches and alerts on logs, Cloud Profiler shows where code consumes resources, Error Reporting surfaces failures, and Cloud Trace follows a single request along its path, which is the only one of them that shows where time is spent between services that each look healthy alone.

distractors.A: Per-service metrics are what the dashboards already show, and they report every service inside its limits, which is how a chain can be slow while no link in it is.
distractors.B: Searching logs service by service can reconstruct part of a journey by hand, and nothing joins those entries into one request's path.
distractors.D: Profiling shows where one service's code spends resources, which is the next question to ask once the slow step in the chain has been identified.

questions.question: A ferry and port operator's booking platform runs redundant instances spread across three zones and takes nightly backups, all inside one region. The board has set a new requirement: a ticket must still be sellable if that entire region is lost. Which change meets the requirement?

options.A: Add more zones within the same region so the redundancy across the platform is deeper
options.B: Replicate into a second region, with traffic routed to whichever is healthy
options.C: Increase the backup frequency to hourly so less is lost when the region fails
options.D: Publish a service level agreement committing to a stated recovery time

rationale.correct: Redundancy, replication, scalable infrastructure and backups are the design moves, while reliability, high availability and operational excellence are the commitments those moves deliver. A design that never leaves one region survives nothing regional however many zones it spans, so meeting this requirement means replication into a second region with traffic able to reach it.

distractors.A: Zones are subdivisions of a region, so adding more of them deepens redundancy inside the very failure domain the requirement says can be lost.
distractors.C: More frequent backups shrink how much data is lost and keep no tickets selling, as a backup still has to be restored somewhere that is running.
distractors.D: A published commitment states what the operator promises, and the platform's ability to keep selling through a regional loss is unchanged by the promise.

questions.question: A recycling cooperative's collection app measures the share of booking requests completed in under one second. Its platform team has committed internally to holding that share above a stated level, and the cooperative's contract with the councils it serves promises a credit if the share falls below a lower level. Which terms name those three things, in that order?

options.A: Service level agreement, service level objective, service level indicator
options.B: Saturation, latency and traffic, the signals that each of these terms measures
options.C: All three are service level objectives, differing only in who is told
options.D: Service level indicator, service level objective, service level agreement

rationale.correct: The three terms are told apart by who they bind. A service level indicator measures something, and the share of bookings completed in under one second is a measurement. A service level objective commits the team to a target for that measurement. A service level agreement commits the business to its customer, with a consequence attached. Latency, traffic, saturation and errors are the signals an indicator can be built from.

distractors.A: This reverses the order: the measurement comes first, the internal target sits on top of it, and the external promise carrying a consequence comes last.
distractors.B: Latency, traffic, saturation and errors name what can be measured, and the question asks what the measurement, the internal target and the external promise are called.
distractors.C: An objective binds the team while an agreement binds the business to its customer with a consequence, so collapsing the three loses the distinction that matters when a credit is owed.
